Boiler services for heat problems

Boiler services for cold rooms, noise or leaks.

A basement boiler can be running while an upstairs apartment stays cold. These symptoms help describe the problem at booking. Observations are useful; pressure changes, hot fittings and repeated resets belong with the technician.

Boiler runs, but several radiators stay cold Call today Access affects timing

Likely causes

  • A stopped circulator or an air bound hot-water loop.
  • Flooded steam returns.
  • A failed radiator air vent.

Check safely first

  • List cold rooms and affected floors.
  • Read the thermostat without opening equipment.
  • Note whether the boiler runs.

What the technician does

Prompt service if rooms are losing heat. The technician traces heat delivery to the affected rooms. The diagnosis separates a building-wide supply problem from a fault at one radiator.

One radiator stays cold while nearby rooms warm Book soon Local fault assessment

Likely causes

  • Trapped air in a hot-water radiator.
  • A partly closed radiator valve.
  • A failed steam radiator air vent.

Check safely first

  • Record the room, time and whether one radiator stays cold throughout a heating cycle.
  • Compare the cold radiator with warm rooms.
  • Keep furniture clear of radiators.
  • Leave unfamiliar valves and hot fittings alone.

What the technician does

Book service before the room becomes too cold. The technician compares the cold radiator with the operating system. Local repairs should address the cause without disrupting heat for other apartments.

Banging begins when steam heat starts Book soon Drainage assessment

Likely causes

  • Condensate trapped by poorly pitched piping.
  • A radiator that cannot drain.
  • Flooded steam returns.

Check safely first

  • Locate the noise from a safe distance.
  • Record when banging occurs.
  • Avoid touching hot pipes.
  • Leave pressure and piping adjustments to the technician.

What the technician does

Arrange diagnosis if banging is new, forceful or getting worse. The technician checks steam delivery and water return at the noisy branch. A replacement part alone may leave a drainage problem unresolved.

Water appears beside the boiler Call today Leak source assessment

Likely causes

  • A leaking pipe connection.
  • A relief valve discharging.
  • A cracked boiler section.

Check safely first

  • Describe the leak from a dry position.
  • Note whether water appears during operation.
  • Do not open covers, tighten fittings or refill.

What the technician does

Prompt assessment; keep clear of hot water and wet electrical equipment. The technician identifies the leak source. A leaking connection and a leaking boiler body can lead to different repair decisions.

Boiler starts and stops without warming the building Call today Heating cycle observation

Likely causes

  • A low water cutoff interrupting operation.
  • A faulty thermostat or operating control.
  • A stopped circulator causing poor heat delivery.

Check safely first

  • Record how often the boiler stops.
  • Read visible messages without opening panels.
  • Do not repeatedly reset or bypass safety devices.

What the technician does

Prompt service when repeated stops leave rooms cold. The technician traces the stop condition through a heating cycle. Restarting the boiler alone does not explain why operation ended.

Steam radiator hisses for too long or spits water Call today Shared fault assessment

Likely causes

  • A radiator air vent that cannot close.
  • Condensate trapped at the radiator.
  • Excess water or pressure in the steam system.

Check safely first

  • Keep clear of escaping steam or hot water; identify the affected room from a safe distance.
  • Note whether other radiators are affected.
  • Do not cover openings or remove hot parts.

What the technician does

Keep clear of escaping steam or hot water; arrange service. The technician checks the radiator and wider steam system. Similar complaints in several rooms may indicate a shared fault.

Likely causes

  • A leaking pipe connection.
  • An expansion tank fault on a hot-water system.

Check safely first

  • Record the reading if safely visible.
  • Note changes during operation.
  • Report any water near the boiler.
  • Leave filling, draining and adjustments to the technician.

Likely causes

  • A thermostat that is not calling for heat.
  • A low water cutoff or ignition fault.
  • A stopped circulator or blocked steam return.

Check safely first

  • Check the thermostat display and setting.
  • List occupied rooms without heat.
  • Do not relight or repeatedly reset equipment.
  • For gas odors or CO alarms, leave and call emergency services from outside.

Call promptly; report gas odors or a CO alarm as an emergency. The technician separates a boiler shutdown from a distribution fault. Report building-wide heat loss at booking so the scope is clear.

What shapes boiler services pricing? The work and the building.

2 Steam or hot-water operationThe system type changes the diagnostic path and parts involved. Steam complaints may involve air release and water return. Hot-water complaints may involve circulation. The boiler services quote should match the equipment.

Boiler services in Chicago: common questions

What fixes a boiler that fires but leaves the house cold?

A boiler that fires but leaves rooms cold usually has a distribution fault. On a hot water system that means an air bound loop, a stopped circulator or a closed valve. On steam it means flooded returns and air vents that cannot breathe. Diagnosis starts on the water side and the controls, not the burner. Pressure, water level and the operating control settings decide whether heat reaches the radiators. City & Suburban staffs NATE-certified technicians, repairs all makes and models, and shows the fault before quoting a price.

Boiler services pricing depends on the visit scope, including annual boiler maintenance or a diagnosed repair. Cost follows the part that failed and the work needed to reach it. A radiator vent or a thermocouple on an accessible steam boiler sits at one end of the range. A leaking section, a seized circulator, a failed gas valve or a control board on a wall hung boiler sits at the other. Age matters, because a boiler built decades ago may need a special order control. Access matters too: a crawlspace or a locked shared basement adds time. What happens during a boiler services visit?

A boiler repair visit starts with the complaint, the thermostat and the boiler controls. Gas pressure and ignition are checked next. On a steam boiler the low water cutoff and gauge glass may be checked, as the equipment allows. On a hot water system the relief valve, expansion tank and circulator may be inspected. Water level, pressure and flue condition are recorded. A repair that uses a part on hand may be finished the same visit, while a special order control means a return trip. City & Suburban explains the fault and the options at the boiler, and the price is written down before work is authorized.

Which boiler symptoms should not wait until morning?

Four symptoms qualify: a gas smell, a carbon monoxide alarm sounding, water pouring from the boiler or a relief valve discharging, and no heat at all in freezing weather. A gas smell means leaving the building and calling the gas utility or 911 from outside. A carbon monoxide alarm means getting everyone outside and calling 911 from there, without stopping to switch equipment off. For water or a discharging relief valve, keep clear of hot water and wet electrical equipment, leave valves and the water feed alone, and call for service. City & Suburban offers emergency HVAC service every day till midnight, except Sundays, and same day service when the schedule allows. Knocking pipes, a short cycling burner or one cold radiator can wait for a scheduled heater repair visit.

How can annual boiler maintenance help address radiator heat problems?

Annual boiler maintenance is a chance to discuss radiator heat before winter. On a hot water loop, a single cold radiator can come from trapped air, a partly closed valve or a restricted branch. On a steam system, possible causes include a failed air vent on that radiator, a failed thermostatic valve, or a pitch problem that lets condensate pool in the pipe. Bleeding a radiator and handling hot valves or fittings is technician work. A whole floor going cold points somewhere else: the boiler, the circulator, or steam pressure set too high for the pipe runs. What does the Chicago Heat Ordinance require of a building heated by a boiler?

The Chicago Municipal Code sets a heating season from September 15 to June 1. Where the landlord supplies the heat, the general rule is at least 68 degrees from 8:30 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. and at least 66 degrees overnight. The code also lists exceptions (Chicago Municipal Code 13-196-410). In a two-flat with one boiler that duty belongs to the owner, not the tenant, so a stopped circulator becomes a compliance problem overnight. Does the age of a boiler put a repair out of reach?

Rarely, and not because of age alone. Cast iron sectional boilers from the middle of the last century still run in Chicago. The heat exchanger is heavy and the controls are simple. What ends a boiler is a cracked or leaking section, a flooded burner tray, or a flue that cannot be made safe. Controls, vents, circulators and gas valves are still sold or have modern equivalents. A boiler suits the building it was designed for: radiators, solid masonry walls, and rooms that hold steady heat without blowing dust around. A home that also wants cooling does not have to give up radiator heat: ductless cooling or a separate air conditioning system can run alongside the boiler, and those options are worth comparing before any conversion. A converted attic or rear addition that was never piped for heat may be better served by a separate system such as a heat pump. What safety devices belong in a house heated by a boiler?

A working carbon monoxide alarm comes first. Illinois requires alarms near sleeping areas in dwellings under the Carbon Monoxide Alarm Detector Act (430 ILCS 135). On the boiler the safety chain is the pressure relief valve, the low water cutoff on a steam system, and the flue that carries combustion gases outside. A relief valve that weeps or a cutoff that has never been blown down is a reason to shut the boiler off and call. Rust flakes under the flue hood are another. A boiler services visit tests those controls. City & Suburban repairs all makes and models and shows what failed before quoting a price.

What does annual boiler maintenance include that a furnace tune-up does not?

Water. Depending on the equipment and manufacturer instructions, annual maintenance on a steam boiler can include testing the low water cutoff (blowing it down where it is a blow-down type), checking the gauge glass and testing the relief valve, with operating pressure checked against the system design. Skimming a boiler that makes wet steam is a corrective task once diagnosed, not an automatic annual step. A hot water system instead calls for checks of the expansion tank charge, the circulator and the air separator. The written scope should say which tasks apply. None of that exists on a furnace, which is why heater maintenance is a separate visit with a separate checklist. Component repairs generally do not. Replacing the equipment does, because installed heating equipment is permitted work in Chicago. City of Chicago building permit records for the 24 months to August 2026 mention 108 boiler permits, a small share next to furnace work. A permit adds inspection time to the schedule, and the cost sits inside the written price rather than beside it. Boiler replacements in Chicago generally need a City permit, and the written quote should say who pulls it. City & Suburban repairs all makes and models and prices upfront with no hidden fees.

What should a Chicago homeowner ask before booking steam boiler services?

Five questions sort the field. Ask how many steam systems a contractor works on in a Chicago winter, because one-pipe steam behaves nothing like a hot water loop. Ask whether the person who diagnoses the fault is the person who sells the replacement. Ask for the exact price in writing before work starts. Ask whether repairs cover all makes and models, which decides who can touch a cast iron boiler. Ask for license and insurance details. What keeps a boiler and radiator system out of trouble between seasons?

Four habits. Book annual service before September 15, when the Chicago Heat Ordinance season starts and many contractors take the first cold calls at once. Keep furniture, covers and curtains clear of radiators so heat reaches the room. Report a new noise, a weeping valve or a cold radiator while the weather is still mild and the schedule is open. Keep working carbon monoxide alarms near sleeping areas; the Illinois Carbon Monoxide Alarm Detector Act requires an operating alarm within 15 feet of each sleeping room in the dwellings it covers. Boiler services for cold rooms, noise or leaks.

A basement boiler can be running while an upstairs apartment stays cold. These symptoms help describe the problem at booking. Observations are useful; pressure changes, hot fittings and repeated resets belong with the technician.

Boiler runs, but several radiators stay cold Call today Access affects timing

Likely causes

  • A stopped circulator or an air bound hot-water loop.
  • Flooded steam returns.
  • A failed radiator air vent.

Check safely first

  • List cold rooms and affected floors.
  • Read the thermostat without opening equipment.
  • Note whether the boiler runs.

What the technician does

Prompt service if rooms are losing heat. The technician traces heat delivery to the affected rooms. The diagnosis separates a building-wide supply problem from a fault at one radiator.

Likely causes

  • A partly closed radiator valve.
  • A failed steam radiator air vent.

Check safely first

  • Record the room, time and whether one radiator stays cold throughout a heating cycle.
  • Compare the cold radiator with warm rooms.
  • Keep furniture clear of radiators.
  • Leave unfamiliar valves and hot fittings alone.

  • Locate the noise from a safe distance.
  • Record when banging occurs.
  • Avoid touching hot pipes.

  • Note whether water appears during operation.

  • Record how often the boiler stops.
  • Read visible messages without opening panels.

  • A radiator air vent that cannot close.
  • Condensate trapped at the radiator.
  • Excess water or pressure in the steam system.

  • Keep clear of escaping steam or hot water; identify the affected room from a safe distance.
  • Note whether other radiators are affected.
  • Do not cover openings or remove hot parts.

Likely causes

  • A leaking pipe connection.
  • An expansion tank fault on a hot-water system.

  • Note changes during operation.
  • Report any water near the boiler.
  • Leave filling, draining and adjustments to the technician.

  • A faulty thermostat or zone control.
  • A steam vent or return fault on one branch.

Check safely first

  • Record apartment temperatures and times.
  • Coordinate access with the building contact.
  • List recent changes to affected rooms.
  • Leave shared controls unchanged without building authorization.

Prioritize a cold occupied apartment during heating season. The technician compares warm and cold apartments. Access to both floors helps avoid a diagnosis based only on basement observations.

The entire building has no boiler heat Emergency Confirm service availability

Likely causes

  • A thermostat that is not calling for heat.
  • A low water cutoff or ignition fault.
  • A stopped circulator or blocked steam return.

Check safely first

  • Check the thermostat display and setting.
  • List occupied rooms without heat.
  • Do not relight or repeatedly reset equipment.
  • For gas odors or CO alarms, leave and call emergency services from outside.

What the technician does

Call promptly; report gas odors or a CO alarm as an emergency. The technician separates a boiler shutdown from a distribution fault. Report building-wide heat loss at booking so the scope is clear.

  • •Visible messages or readings, recorded from a safe position. Leave equipment closed.
  • •The building contact and access arrangements for the basement and affected apartments.

  • •Hot-water boiler services follow circulation through the building. A circulator moves heated water while an expansion tank accommodates changes as water warms. Cast iron sectional and wall hung boilers have different controls and service access.

What fixes a boiler that fires but leaves the house cold?

A boiler that fires but leaves rooms cold usually has a distribution fault. On a hot water system that means an air bound loop, a stopped circulator or a closed valve. On steam it means flooded returns and air vents that cannot breathe. Diagnosis starts on the water side and the controls, not the burner. A boiler repair visit starts with the complaint, the thermostat and the boiler controls. Gas pressure and ignition are checked next. Which boiler symptoms should not wait until morning?

Four symptoms qualify: a gas smell, a carbon monoxide alarm sounding, water pouring from the boiler or a relief valve discharging, and no heat at all in freezing weather. A gas smell means leaving the building and calling the gas utility or 911 from outside. A carbon monoxide alarm means getting everyone outside and calling 911 from there, without stopping to switch equipment off. For water or a discharging relief valve, keep clear of hot water and wet electrical equipment, leave valves and the water feed alone, and call for service. Annual boiler maintenance is a chance to discuss radiator heat before winter. On a hot water loop, a single cold radiator can come from trapped air, a partly closed valve or a restricted branch. On a steam system, possible causes include a failed air vent on that radiator, a failed thermostatic valve, or a pitch problem that lets condensate pool in the pipe. The Chicago Municipal Code sets a heating season from September 15 to June 1.
